hero.title: The Pancha Sila of Buddhism
hero.description: The foundational ethical code of Buddhism, known as the five precepts (Pancha Sila), guiding the moral conduct of lay followers.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Ahimsa (Non-violence)
  • Asteya (Non-stealing)
  • Brahmacharya (Chastity)
  • Satya (Truthfulness)
  • Surameraya (No Intoxicants)

Target Audience

  • Upasaka: Lay male followers
  • Upasika: Lay female followers
  • Sangha: The monastic community (followed additional precepts)

Structure of the Five Precepts

  • 1. Panatipata Veramani: Abstaining from taking life.
  • 2. Adinnadana Veramani: Abstaining from taking what is not given.
  • 3. Kamesu Micchacara Veramani: Abstaining from sexual misconduct.
  • 4. Musavada Veramani: Abstaining from false speech.
  • 5. Surameraya Majjapamadatthana Veramani: Abstaining from intoxicants.

cards.details: Life of Siddhartha Gautama. The formulation of the Noble Eightfold Path and the specific ethical precepts for the Sangha and laity.
Ashoka the Great institutionalizes Dhamma, effectively promoting the Pancha Sila as state-mandated moral guidelines for subjects.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Remember the 5 Sila using the keyword 'V-I-L-L-A'

items.title: V-I-L-L-A
items.decryption: The 5 Sila are prohibitions against: Violence (Life), Larceny (Theft), Adultery (Sexual misconduct), Lying (False speech), and Intoxication.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Mistaking Pancha Sila for the 'Pancha Mahavrata' of Jainism; while overlapping, Jain principles are far more ascetic and rigid.
Confusing 'Pancha Sila' with the 'Pancha Sheel' treaty of 1954 (Nehru-Zhou Enlai) which is modern diplomatic history, not Ancient history.
Assuming these apply only to monks; they are primarily meant for 'Upasakas' (lay followers).
